result.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
result.summary: Humans explore unfamiliar spaces with purpose, deciding where to look until they have gathered the evidence a spatial question requires. However, can vision-language models (VLMs), which reason increasingly well over curated images and videos, also seek in space when the evidence is not handed to them? We present ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark of 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, where a model starts from a single view, navigates real captured frames, and must gather evidence before answering. To assess whether such exploration is purposeful, we introduce a controlled evaluation protocol that fixes each model as the reasoner and compares its own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route, separating evidence seeking from spatial reasoning. Every question is verified to require exploration and answered from 3D annotations, masked-evidence questions test whether models know when to abstain, and over 95% of sampled questions are confirmed correct by human verification. Evaluations of 23 proprietary, open-weight, and spatially specialized VLMs reveal that the strongest models do seek evidence with purpose but lose much of it to limited memory, whereas weaker and specialized models explore no better than a random walk or fail to reason over the evidence they are given, pointing to memory and evidence-grounded reasoning as the next targets for active spatial intelligence.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ActSpace-Bench：在 72 个真实扫描室内场景、234 个探索回合和 994 个问题上，让 VLM 从单视角出发主动导航取帧、收集证据后作答，并用同预算随机游走与 oracle 路线分离「找证据」和「空间推理」，评测了 23 个模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LOOK/STOP 的收益与成本、证据获取与推理的贡献分解，以及掩蔽证据下的弃答判断；其「强模型受限于记忆、弱模型不优于随机游走」的结论可供核查探索轨迹中证据保留与视觉旁路问题。
